entries.feature: Write and run your own indicators
entries.note: Saved scripts go on the chart as script indicators run on the server in worker processes (time limit, per-user runs, shared result cache): plot (line, histogram, circles), plotshape, plotchar, plotarrow, bgcolor, barcolor, hline, and line, box and label drawings, with per-bar colours; inputs edit in the indicator settings; layouts keep them. Not drawn yet (the console says so): fill, plotcandle, plotbar, table; request.security and strategy() are outside the subset (OMNIX_SCRIPTS_SPEC.md). A forming bar re-runs at most every 5 s.

CodeMirror 6: Pine-compatible highlighting, completion of the interpreter's functions, constants and variables, hover with parameters, inline problems from the server compiler as you type; save, save as, import and export (.pine), add to or update on the chart.

Each save with a new source or name is a version (migration 0145, written in the save's transaction, 200 kept); the History tab diffs a version against the editor or the version before and restores it.

Alerts on a script indicator's plots, alertcondition() conditions and alert() calls, evaluated by the server's alert monitor with the browser closed: the alert keeps the script version saved when it was made and runs it in a script worker on the monitor's bars. Without a message of its own, the trigger says what alert() or the alertcondition says (placeholders filled). Not on watchlist alerts.

strategy() scripts with strategy.entry/order/exit/close/close_all/cancel, brackets with trailing stops, OCA, pyramiding, commission and slippage, filled like TradingView's broker emulator (OHLC bar path). The Strategy Tester shows overview (equity vs buy and hold, drawdown), performance summary (all/long/short, Sharpe, Sortino), list of trades and properties, and a deep backtest over up to 20,000 bars of the provider's history; fills are drawn on the chart. Research only: a simulated account, never an order; the roadmap's optional paper-signal link is not built. Omnix's own strategies stay Python with their own backtester.
The console shows log.info/warning/error with their bar, run and compile errors, and what the chart couldn't draw; the profiler shows time per line in a table and beside the code.

Outbox written with the trigger, retries with backoff, HMAC signature. The alert dialog sets the URL and optional signing secret (write-only; a stored webhook shows only its host). The body is the message with placeholders filled, sent as JSON when it parses as JSON.

entries.feature: Moving up/down by amount or % within N bars
Alerts on any indicator and any output line
entries.note: The chart's alert dialog offers the chart's indicators, each with its output lines, and a comparison (crossing, crossing up or down, greater or less than) against a value. The alert is a conditions alert, which the server evaluates on its own bars with the same inputs. Indicators the server can't evaluate, or whose extra inputs it doesn't take yet (TradingView-style parameters, a compare symbol), are greyed out with the reason. A cross-language contract test checks that every line offered for the 109 server indicators is a server output. The alerts list panel keeps the legacy indicator list.

entries.feature: Alerts on horizontal lines/rays, rectangles, channels, fib levels
entries.note: Line alerts from horizontal lines and rays, trend lines, rays and extended lines, parallel and other channels, rectangles (top and bottom) and fib retracement levels; the dialog picks the level. An alert follows its drawing: once a moved drawing settles on the active chart (not in replay), the alert takes the level's new line; lines are compared as the server evaluates them, so charts on other intervals agree. Deleting the drawing on its chart, or a level that goes away (fib levels are keyed by value), asks on the active chart whether to disable its alerts; Keep is remembered until the page reloads. The server evaluates a line extended both ways, so a rectangle edge or a fib level also alerts past the drawing's right edge (levels that only extend back in time are not offered). Choosing the level in edit mode is a follow-up.

The server fills {{ticker}}, {{exchange}}, {{interval}}, {{open}}, {{high}}, {{low}}, {{close}}, {{volume}}, {{time}}, {{timenow}}, {{alert_name}}, {{plot_N}} and {{plot("name")}} when the alert triggers, and stores the result with the trigger, so the app, the toast and the webhook show the same text. Unknown placeholders stay as written. The dialog lists the placeholders. {{plot_N}} is the value watched by condition N.

Email through the workspace's SMTP server (STARTTLS or TLS; the password in the OS-protected secret store; the server's address checked like a webhook's) and web push to every device that allowed notifications (RFC 8291 encryption, VAPID; an OS notification even with Omnix closed, a click brings Omnix forward). Both go through the alert outbox with retries; the dialog sets them up inline with test sends. The secret store is DPAPI, so on another OS the password and VAPID key need a portable store first (TVP-0.5a's note).

Up to 5 conditions combined with AND, one frequency and one message. The dialog edits each condition (price fields, change %, chart indicator lines; crossing, greater/less than, channel, moving by an amount or percent within bars); adding conditions to a price, volume, change or chart-indicator alert makes it a conditions alert with its own condition first. Drawing alerts keep one condition (they follow their drawing). Evaluated on the server (TVP-1.2), all on the closed bar for once-per-bar-close.

entries.feature: Watchlist alerts (one alert over a whole list)
entries.note: An alert's "Applies to" picks a watchlist: one definition (price, indicator or change conditions; no trendlines) evaluated on each of the list's symbols, read at every pass, with its own trigger state per symbol (once, cooldown, history; re-enabling re-arms every symbol). Symbols evaluated: the alert's limit (default 100, at most 1,000), within one request budget per pass shared by all alerts: half of each provider's budget (Alpaca about 45 fetches, Binance 600 at a 30 s pass), 25 a pass for Yahoo, which publishes none; the dialog estimates it and the monitor's diagnostics show each list alert's evaluated and skipped symbols. One history fetch per symbol per pass, shared with that symbol's own alerts, rather than TradingView's 1,000-symbol lists.

entries.note: Filters and columns on any server registry indicator and line (with its period); price, change % over N bars, volume, relative volume, gap %, and distance from the N-bar high or low (252 bars on daily is the 52-week high or low); SMA, EMA, RSI, ATR. Market cap and fundamentals wait for TVP-10.2, breadth for TVP-6.6.

Rules can be filters or columns, and every rule is a result column. Columns sort by clicking their header. Saved screens load into the editor and save back at their revision. A result's symbol opens on the active chart (and its colour link group), and results can be added to the open watchlist.

A saved screen re-runs every 10 s or every minute while the screener is open. A new run starts only when none of its runs is working, and the server bounds each run. Results new since the previous run are highlighted, and the screen says how many are new or dropped.

US stocks: the 300 most traded active NYSE and Nasdaq stocks (Alpaca snapshots), grouped by sector from SEC SIC codes (coarser than GICS, D-3; filled a few per request, so new names show as unclassified at first) and sized by market cap (SEC shares outstanding times price) or dollar volume. Crypto: the 100 most traded Binance USDT pairs by 24-hour volume (market caps would need CoinMarketCap). Coloured by the day's change; a tile opens its symbol on the chart.

Describe a screen in words; the research model (the Hermes research provider, a versioned prompt) proposes screener rules from the scanner's metrics and the registry's indicators, every rule is checked by the scanner's own validation, and the rules fill the editor for the user to change, save and run. The model sees only the description and the indicator catalog, never market data or symbols, and nothing runs without the user. Comparing two lines (close above its 200-day average) is not a screener rule yet and is reported as not covered.

entries.feature: Update interval (sub-bar playback, down to 1 s)
entries.note: Update interval from 1m to 4h where it fits the chart interval (the providers' bars start at one minute, so no seconds): the shared clock steps by it, skipping the time between bars, and every chart draws its forming bar from intrabar data (TVP-0.6 loader), in the sessions the chart shows. Intrabar data reaches back 5,000 lower bars from now; older replays say where it starts. Replay orders fill on whole bars, so they are placed at bar closes.

entries.feature: Jump to bar during playback; jump to real time

entries.note: Shift+Down plays or pauses, Shift+Right and Shift+Left step; rebindable in the shortcut dialog.

entries.feature: Multiple paper accounts with custom starting cash
OCO stop-loss / take-profit for long positions

entries.note: Accounts have a shorting setting: on by default in the account form, off for accounts created without it, including strategy accounts. It can be changed in the account settings, at the account's revision. On such an account, a sell with nothing long held is a short entry. The server sizes it from its risk, with a stop above the entry, through the same manual-risk order path as a long entry. Without a margin model (TVP-7.2b), a short is capped at the cash buying power.

A short entry's stop (above) and target (below) are armed with it. The protection monitor triggers them mirrored and covers with a reduce-only buy. A trailing stop trails above the lowest price. Short positions and entries count toward the account's open risk.

The replay backtest has an Allow short option. With it, a cross down closes a long and opens a short, and a cross up covers and goes long. Long-only results are unchanged. Before this, backtest.py refused allow_short.

entries.feature: Leverage per asset class and margin % for longs and shorts
entries.note: Margin % per asset class for longs and shorts (the account dialog's leverage ratios, with Margin control on): a leveraged buy holds its margin share and borrows the rest; buying power (equity less margin and holds, at market) and the risk preview count it. 100% (no leverage) by default, so existing and strategy-owned long accounts are unchanged. Replay trading stays on cash alone.

entries.feature: Margin calls (forced partial or full liquidation)
entries.note: The paper monitor prices every position of accounts using leverage or holding shorts; when equity is below the maintenance (the margin %, at market), it closes the positions using the most margin first, only as far as needed, with reducing market orders shown as margin calls, cancelling only the working orders on the closing side it needs to. A cancelled or rejected margin call is followed by a new one. Note: accounts that already hold shorts are now margin-called at 100% short margin (D-2). Shown on the account, not sent through the alert outbox.
Commission type Percent (bps of the notional) or Fixed (an amount once per order, on its first fill), in the account dialog; replay uses it too.
DAY expiry for futures/forex at venue close and the new order types in replay are follow-ups.

entries.feature: Drag orders and brackets on the chart
entries.note: Working orders are drawn as lines showing side, type and quantity. Drag a line and press Move to re-price the order, or cancel it from the line. A buy entry is re-priced by the server: it is re-sized to the same risk and replaced atomically, and its pending stop and target move with it. A sell is replaced with the same order at the new price. A position's or working entry's stop and target are dragged from the position overlay. Trailing stops are not draggable: they move by themselves.

A "+" beside the price scale at the pointer's price offers a buy limit or sell stop below the market, a sell limit or buy stop above it, and Add alert. Orders fill the paper ticket (decision TVP-7.3).

entries.feature: Buy/sell buttons in the chart legend
entries.note: Sell and Buy buttons show the bid and ask (the last price without a book, and in replay) and the spread. They fill the paper ticket with a market order.

Paper accounts only, while the paper ticket is open. Deliberate difference from TradingView (decision TVP-7.4): the keys fill the ticket and the user places the order; TradingView places at the default quantity unless confirmation is on. Order authority stays with the server (buys are risk-sized and need a stop; sells reduce a long).

entries.feature: Trading notifications on chart and notifications log
entries.note: Fills, rejections, cancellations and expiries as a toast over the chart and in the dock's Notifications tab. Margin calls arrive with TVP-7.2b.
None exists; the 'prospective' side tab is the prospective economic-SHADOW strategy panel. US releases can come from FRED's release calendar (§7.2); TVP-10.5.

entries.feature: Analyst price targets and dividend yield
Earnings and dividends calendar, chart markers
entries.note: Earnings appear only as catalyst research facts, and dividend yield as an indicator; no calendar view or chart markers.

For US filers, from SEC XBRL company facts (D-5): income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, annual and quarterly (year-to-date and fourth quarters derived), and ratios on the trailing twelve months (P/E, P/S, P/B, margins, ROE, ROA, current ratio, debt to equity, revenue and EPS growth). Non-US (IFRS) issuers and charting a fundamental as an indicator are not covered.

entries.feature: Options chain, Greeks, volatility curves, strategy builder
Macro: yield curves, economic indicators, maps
Up to 12 tabs in one browser tab
Open a layout in a new window
entries.note: A workspace (header button) or a tab (tab menu, new-tab launcher) opens in a new browser window, an ordinary Omnix page on that workspace and tab. Windows announce saves on a BroadcastChannel: a window without edits of its own reloads a workspace or watchlist another one saved, keeping its replay, closed tabs and shown tab; an edit made meanwhile meets the revision conflict prompt. Alert sounds and toasts play only in the most recently focused Trading window (windows that leave, crash or freeze stop counting). Needs a visual check in two real windows.

entries.feature: Full multi-window (pop out tabs, move them between windows)

entries.note: Duplicate from the tab menu (right-click or the tab's ... button) or the new-tab launcher, with the tab's drawings; reopen closed tab (the last 10) from the menus or the keyboard.

entries.feature: New-tab launcher (open a saved layout or tool)
entries.note: The + button opens a launcher: new chart tab, duplicate this tab, reopen closed tab, open this tab in a new window, saved layouts (workspaces), and tools (screener, backtest and replay, strategies, paper trading). Keyboard: arrows, Escape. Needs a visual check.
Closing or reloading the page while edits are unsaved (draft, saving or conflict) asks first; drafts are also recovered after a reload.

entries.feature: Installable app (own window, taskbar icon, OS notifications)
entries.note: Installs from the browser as Omnix Trading (web app manifest, own window and taskbar icon, decision D-8); the shortcut dialog offers the browser's install prompt. OS notifications come from web push (TVP-0.5c), with Omnix open or closed. The app's scope is the whole site, so other Omnix pages opened from it stay in its window. A visual check in an installed window is still worth doing.
